refuted_or_corrected.claim: Whisper large-v3-turbo on Databricks Custom LLM Serving is a 'Documented GA path (2026 docs)' (asr-serving option A maturity).
refuted_or_corrected.correction: The Custom LLM serving page (updated Nov 11 2026) is labeled Public Preview, and a workspace admin has to enable it on the Previews page. Only the GPU_MEDIUM (A10G) workload type is called 'Generally available'. The rest checks out: Whisper large-v3-turbo is an official starter, llm/v1/audio/transcriptions and llm/v1/audio/translations are supported tasks, and AI Runtime, MLflow 3.12+ and databricks-sdk 0.102.0+ are required. The 'Databricks ASR' enterprise default therefore depends on a Preview feature plus an admin toggle.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: FMAPI/AI Gateway has no audio path, so cloud ASR needs a custom GPU endpoint or a non-governed vendor API (asr-serving option D and governance requirement; the slm-cleanup tier also assumes text-only).
refuted_or_corrected.correction: Databricks documents audio input to Gemini pay-per-token models through Unity Gateway. You send it with the Chat Completions API (content type audio_url, either a URL or a base64 data URI) or with the native Gemini API (inlineData). The page lists databricks-gemini-3-1-pro, databricks-gemini-3-1-flash-lite and databricks-gemini-3-flash as supported; the Gemini API page also names gemini-3-5-flash-lite. This gives Mog a governed, pay-per-token option with no GPU to manage, where one call does 'transcribe + clean up'. Caveats: global endpoint or cross-geo routing is required, provisioned throughput is not supported, the 4 MB FMAPI payload limit applies, and latency is unbenchmarked. The external-models claim itself is correct: external endpoints list only completions, chat and embeddings tasks.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: Gemini Flash-Lite on Databricks is reasoning-heavy (4-5 s TTFT), and GPT models are 'reasoning-only on Databricks', so they are unsuitable for the hot path.
refuted_or_corrected.correction: Gemini 3, 3.1 Flash-Lite and 3.5 Flash/Flash-Lite accept reasoning_effort='minimal', which according to the docs returns no reasoning tokens. Gemini 3.7 and 3.8 Flash do NOT accept 'minimal'. The GPT-6 family (databricks-gpt-6-luna, gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-1-terra/sol) accepts reasoning_effort='none'. GPT-6 Luna is described as the fast, cost-efficient model and is on the priority pay-per-token list. Only the GPT-5.x family rejects none and minimal. So there are low-latency, priority-tier-capable cleanup candidates that the slm-cleanup agent left out.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: Qwen3-Next 80B A3B Instruct: endpoint name, availability and status unverified, 'Listed... Details unverified'.
refuted_or_corrected.correction: The model is in Public Preview (the limits page calls it Beta). The endpoint name is databricks-qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct and the service name is system.ai.qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct. Input is text only and max output is 10,000 tokens. Treat it as a preview dependency.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: Gemini 3.6 Flash and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 'retire Nov 19, 2026', implying hard breakage.
refuted_or_corrected.correction: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash retires on Nov 19 2026. For Gemini 3.6 Flash, calls are automatically redirected to Gemini 3.8 Flash at the same price from that date, so it does not hard-fail, but behavior changes: 3.8 Flash rejects reasoning_effort 'minimal'. GLM 5.2 retires Feb 4 2027 (confirmed). The 'model as config value' recommendation still stands.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: Genie API throughput is about 5 questions/min per workspace for the free-tier API (about 20/min for the UI), quoted as a planning number in several dimensions.
refuted_or_corrected.correction: The current AWS Genie Agents API page (Nov 5 2026) and the limits page give no numeric Genie throughput. The 5/20 qpm figures appear only in older or localized Microsoft Learn pages, which describe 'Genie API free tier (Public Preview)'. Those same pages also show stale limits (30 tables and 10,000 conversations per space, against 50 and 200,000 now), plus community posts. Present the number as historical, keep the client-side queue and 429 handling, and confirm with the account team. The resources/limits page does list Genie limits of 50 tables, 200,000 conversations per space, 10,000 messages per conversation and 100 instructions per space.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: Managed MCP servers (UC functions, Vector Search, Genie): 50 QPS per workspace, used as a general throughput fact.
refuted_or_corrected.correction: The limits page says '50 queries per second from internal Databricks services to managed MCP servers'. That is traffic from inside Databricks (for example agents on Model Serving), not external desktop clients. It says nothing about a desktop app's Genie throughput.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: OAuth: request least-privilege scopes such as 'genie' plus offline_access on the custom OAuth app (ux-governance SEC-1). Elsewhere: 'all-apis covers genie' is unverified.
refuted_or_corrected.correction: The custom-app-integration API documents supported scopes as only all-apis, sql, offline_access, openid, profile and email. The enable-OAuth page says All APIs is required for non-SQL APIs, while openid, email, profile and offline_access are allowed automatically. Fine-grained scopes like 'genie' are listed on the endpoints, but you cannot register them on a custom app per the docs, so a desktop client has to request all-apis. Least privilege is therefore not achievable through scopes; rely on UC and Genie ACLs instead. Defaults are confirmed: access TTL 60 min, refresh TTL 10,080 min, single-use refresh tokens in Beta, and up to 30 minutes to take effect. Pre-enabled published apps exist only for named partners (dbt, Power BI, Tableau, ChatGPT/Codex, Claude, Claude Code, Cursor), so Mog needs a per-account custom app.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: Model Serving payload limits: 16 MB for custom models, 4 MB for FMAPI/external/agent endpoints, 597 s execution.
refuted_or_corrected.correction: Confirmed on pages updated Nov 13 2026 (16 MB custom, 4 MB agent, 597 s, requests over 1 MB not logged). An added fact: protobuf text and binary inputs allow 256 MiB after decoding, which could suit larger custom-endpoint audio uploads if the endpoint supports it. The custom LLM path that needs this is Public Preview (see above).

refuted_or_corrected.claim: Core Audio process taps require macOS 14.2+; set the minimum to 14.2 (audio-meeting) or 14.4.
refuted_or_corrected.correction: The taps API (AudioHardwareCreateProcessTap) appeared in 14.2, per Apple's sample and Electron PR #49717. AudioCap's README dates the API to 14.4. A 2026 practitioner write-up recommends a deployment target of 14.4 or later because earlier builds land in a different TCC category. Also: the permission is granted only to a stable, signed binary (unsigned builds silently get zeros), and there is NO public API to preflight or request the System Audio Recording permission. Apps use private TCCAccessPreflight/Request with kTCCServiceAudioCapture, or rely on the prompt at first start. Recommend 14.4 as the supported minimum, with 14.2-14.3 as best-effort.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: Electron PR #52914 adds an 'activable' option and reworks focus/blur events for key-but-not-main panels.
refuted_or_corrected.correction: Still open and unmerged (last updated Oct 21 2026). During review the author reverted the global focus/blur routing change and restored the setCollectionBehavior override, so the final scope is narrower than the PR title suggests. Do not plan around it.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: Nemotron Speech Streaming EN 0.6B: the March 2026 checkpoint was trained on about 530k hours.
refuted_or_corrected.correction: The current HF model card says the model was trained on ASRSet, about 250,000 hours of US English. The 80/160/560/1120 ms chunks, the Mar 12 2026 updated checkpoint, and Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming (Jun 4 2026, 40 language-locales) are confirmed.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 handles up to 24 min per pass; longer audio needs VAD segmentation (local-stt, audio-meeting).
refuted_or_corrected.correction: The model card says up to 24 min with full attention (on A100 80GB), or up to 3 hours with local attention (rel_pos_local_attn [256,256]). The 24 min full-attention figure is GPU-memory bound, and on laptops you will hit RAM limits much sooner, so VAD chunking is still advisable. The license is confirmed as CC-BY-4.0 ('ready for commercial/non-commercial use'), with 25 European languages, punctuation and capitalization, and an Aug 14 2025 release. The card now also points to an official NeMo-Speech.cpp GGUF runtime (q8_0), which is another local-runtime option.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: Silero VAD 'v5' should be used for meeting mode (audio-meeting) and 'v6 (Aug 2025)', current v6.2.3 (local-stt).
refuted_or_corrected.correction: The current release line is v6.x: v6.2 shipped Nov 2025 with a reworked training paradigm, v6.2.2 on Sep 17 2026 added an offline 16 kHz sequence ONNX model, and v6.2.3 on Sep 23 2026 made torchaudio optional. Standardize on v6.2.x rather than v5.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: OpenAI whisper-1 / gpt-4o-transcribe deprecated with shutdown Feb 26 2027; Genie user usage free until Jan 31 2027; ai_transcribe Beta, 1 h / 512 MB, EN/ES only; Genie One MCP GA, with the Beta /api/2.0/mcp/genie EOL Nov 30 2026; hotkey_manager 0.4 key-up only on macOS/Wayland; Tauri global-shortcut reports Pressed/Released; Handy ~38.7k stars MIT; sherpa_onnx 2.0.1.
refuted_or_corrected.correction: All confirmed on primary pages. Small notes: the Genie MCP migration requires the 'ai-gateway' OAuth scope instead of 'genie'. sherpa_onnx Flutter lists iOS as arm64 only and does support Web. Tauri global-shortcut needs a non-modifier chord (modifier-only and Fn holds still need a native CGEventTap or WH_KEYBOARD_LL). The '25% promotional discount on billed Genie usage' did not appear on the monitor-cost page and is unverified.

gaps: FMAPI audio input (Gemini via Unity Gateway) gives Mog a governed cloud-ASR tier that needs no GPU and could transcribe and clean up in one call. No agent evaluated it. You need: a latency benchmark for a 5-10 s clip; the base64-plus-JSON size under 4 MB (about 2 min of 16 kHz FLAC or Opus is safe); cross-geo routing approval; and a check on hallucination and verbatim fidelity compared with Whisper/Parakeet. It may be the best 'Databricks ASR' default when local STT is disallowed, ahead of an always-on $1k/month A10G that also depends on a Preview feature.

Custom LLM serving (the Whisper endpoint path) is Public Preview and needs an admin Previews toggle plus AI Runtime. Add this to the admin onboarding checklist next to the Genie One/Agent mode preview toggles.

Hot-path SLM shortlist is missing reasoning-off frontier-small options. Add GPT-6 Luna (reasoning_effort=none, priority tier) and Gemini 3.1/3.5 Flash-Lite (reasoning_effort=minimal, priority tier, global endpoint only) to the eval. Llama 3.1 8B, Gemma 3 12B and Haiku have no priority tier.

Genie Agent mode supports enable_viz (charts), unlike the Genie One API (enable_viz must be false). Agent mode also has a FLASH execution_mode that returns 404 FEATURE_DISABLED when unavailable. The GenieProvider feature detection should treat FLASH availability separately from the preview toggle.

Onboarding for System Audio Recording: there is no public API to check or request kTCCServiceAudioCapture. Mog must either use a private TCC API (an App Review and notarization risk to consider) or detect all-zero buffers after starting the tap. Signed builds are mandatory even in development to test the prompt.

sherpa-onnx v1.13+ macOS builds reportedly bundle an onnxruntime whose CoreML EP needs macOS 14.4+ (MLComputePlan). That aligns with a 14.4 minimum and conflicts with any plan to support macOS 13. This comes from one third-party porting doc and is unverified.
No dimension researched Windows on ARM (Snapdragon) for sherpa-onnx/ONNX Runtime or for low-level keyboard hooks, even though sherpa_onnx lists Windows arm64 and QNN NPU support.

Option+Space is the default global shortcut for the ChatGPT/Codex Pets/Mini AND for Superwhisper. Mog's default hotkey needs a conflict check against those apps' defaults and against Apple's Globe-key dictation.
cross_dimension_conflicts: Desktop stack: desktop-stack recommends Tauri v2 (Rust + React) and argues against Flutter for v1. audio-meeting recommends a Flutter shell with a native C-ABI audio core via dart:ffi. local-stt recommends the sherpa_onnx Flutter FFI package as the single runtime. ux-governance names flutter_secure_storage. The user prefers Flutter. A decision is needed. A native audio/hotkey core with a C ABI works for both shells, so make it the shared foundation whichever shell wins.

Meeting duration policy disagrees. asr-serving: hard cap about 90 min, 3-5 min silence auto-stop. local-stt: 90 min cap, 80 min warning, 10 min silence. audio-meeting: no fixed default (mic-release plus calendar), 15 min silence auto-stop, 4 h hard ceiling. ux-governance: 90 min default with +30 min extension, admin-settable up to 4 h, 10-15 min silence. ai_transcribe caps at 1 h per call. Converge on signal-based stopping with about 15 min silence, a configurable cap (90 min default, admin up to 4 h), and server-side transcription chunked under 1 h.

Live meeting transcription target: audio-meeting sends live VAD chunks to Databricks ASR and says to prefer remote on battery. asr-serving and local-stt default to local Parakeet with an optional final pass. Battery, governance and residency trade-offs need one policy.

SLM call format vs guardrails: slm-cleanup's smart path uses Claude Haiku 5.5 with thinking disabled, which Databricks documents only through the Anthropic Messages API, and it streams tokens. ux-governance SEC-5 says built-in guardrails run only on OpenAI-compatible non-streaming Chat Completions and do not evaluate native Anthropic Messages. You cannot have Haiku-with-thinking-off, streaming, and output PII guardrails all at once.

OAuth scopes: ux-governance asks for least-privilege scopes (for example genie). genie-api assumes all-apis. Custom OAuth apps document only all-apis, sql, offline_access, openid, profile and email. The Genie One MCP path needs ai-gateway. In practice the desktop app will request all-apis plus offline_access.

Genie throughput planning: slm-cleanup and ux-governance treat about 5 qpm per workspace as the operating constraint. genie-api correctly notes current docs publish no number. All dimensions should label it historical or unverified.
Silero VAD version: v5 in audio-meeting vs v6.x in local-stt. Use v6.2.x.
Minimum macOS version: audio-meeting says 14.2 (test 14.2). The desktop stack and practitioner sources point to 14.4 for TCC category and sherpa-onnx CoreML EP reasons.

Cloud ASR default: asr-serving makes an always-on Whisper custom endpoint (about $1k/month, Public Preview) the enterprise default. None of the dimensions considered pay-per-token Gemini audio input via FMAPI, which would change both the cost model and the 'Databricks ASR' recommendation.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: (genie-api, ux-governance SEC-1) A custom public OAuth app can request least-privilege scopes such as 'genie' and 'model-serving'; all-apis is assumed to cover genie.
refuted_or_corrected.correction: The official Custom OAuth App Integration API (GA) lists only these supported scopes: all-apis, sql, offline_access, openid, profile, email. The enable-OAuth docs say any app that calls non-SQL APIs needs all-apis. Fine-grained scopes (genie, model-serving, ai-gateway, sql:restricted-query, etc.) are documented as Databricks Apps user_api_scopes for OBO. A third-party governance reference shows custom app integrations accepting genie, dashboards.genie and model-serving in practice, but that is undocumented. Plan for v1: request all-apis + offline_access, with user_authorized_scopes so the user sees a consent screen. Treat least-privilege scopes as something to test against a real account. If least privilege is a hard requirement, the OBO route through a Databricks App is the only documented way to get it.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: (asr-serving) Desktop auth for the ASR endpoint can use 'workspace OAuth (U2M PKCE via the Databricks CLI/SDK flow)'.
refuted_or_corrected.correction: The databricks-cli client_id is meant for built-in Databricks tools. Third-party tools must register their own custom OAuth app, as the genie-api dimension already notes. Use one Mog-specific public client for ASR, SLM and Genie, so the user signs in once. Use the CLI flow only for dev prototypes.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: (genie-api) Genie latency is unverified; the reference figure is the MCP guidance of 70-260 s per turn.
refuted_or_corrected.correction:
Here are real-world numbers.
- Chat-mode polling: 'anywhere from five seconds to over a minute' (Feb 2026 practitioner write-up).
- GSK production: 34 s average, cut to 22 s with a semantic cache and SQL-template tier in front of Genie, which also took 64% of load off Genie (Aug 2026).
- Genie One MCP: 54.2 s average, 81.9 s worst, 55 polls for 8 questions (Sep 2026).
- Genie on a hard enterprise benchmark: about 100 s average wall time (Databricks blog, Nov 11 2026).

Warehouse start-up also matters, because it shows up in the PENDING_WAREHOUSE status. A serverless SQL warehouse starts in about 2-6 s. Pro/classic takes about 4 minutes. So Mog onboarding should warn when the chosen Genie space uses a non-serverless warehouse. Budget 10-60 s for Chat mode and about 1 min for Genie One, and always run them asynchronously.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: (desktop-stack) Use a listen-only CGEventTap for the Fn/Globe or Right-Option push-to-talk key on macOS.
refuted_or_corrected.correction: A listen-only tap passes Fn through to the OS, which still runs the 'Press 🌐/fn key to' action. Depending on that setting (AppleFnUsageType) the user gets the Emoji viewer, an input-source switch, or Apple Dictation on top of the recording. To swallow Fn you need an active (.defaultTap) tap. In practice an active tap works with only the Accessibility permission, while a listen-only tap needed Input Monitoring, which often needs an app restart (FnFlow/VoiceInk observations). Choosing Apple's 'Press Fn twice' dictation shortcut silently resets the Fn setting. On some external keyboards (e.g. Keychron) Fn is a firmware layer key that the OS never sees. Recommendation: active tap with Accessibility, detect AppleFnUsageType, and offer Right-Cmd or Right-Option fallbacks.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: (slm-cleanup) A local SLM fallback (llama.cpp/MLX 1-4B) has weak quality and should be treated as an experiment.
refuted_or_corrected.correction:
macOS 26: Apple's Foundation Models framework (about 3B parameters, 2-bit, on-device, offline) scored 91.0% on a 300-case dictation-polish benchmark. That compares with 71.7% for Gemma 3n, 51.3% for Llama 3.2 and about 97-99% for cloud mini models, at roughly 0.9 s median latency. Limits:
- Apple Intelligence must be enabled, in a supported region.
- The context window is 4096 tokens. Use a fresh session per call, and prewarm it during recording.
- The custom-adapter API is end-of-life for OS 27. macOS 27 adds a LanguageModel protocol for bring-your-own models.
- It is a Swift API, so Flutter or Tauri needs a native bridge.

Windows: Phi Silica needs package identity (MSIX or a sparse package) and a Limited Access Feature token. It is being replaced by Aion Instruct, with retail rollout in January 2027 and no LAF token needed. So a good offline-cleanup tier is realistic on Apple Silicon now and on Copilot+ PCs from 2027. Generic 1-4B GGUF models remain the weak option.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: (ux-governance) Genie chart rendering has to be built because the viz attachment payload format is unverified.
refuted_or_corrected.correction: The genie-api dimension already found a GA endpoint that downloads a rendered PNG of a viz attachment once the message is COMPLETED (JS SDK downloadMessageAttachmentVisualization). Use that PNG in the v1 card. Build native charts only later. Genie One requires enable_viz=false, so that path is text and tables only.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: (audio-meeting) Use Silero VAD v5.
refuted_or_corrected.correction: Use Silero VAD v6; the current release is v6.2.3 (Sep 2026), with 16% fewer errors on noisy audio. It keeps the 16 kHz input and 512-sample windows. sherpa-onnx and FluidAudio already ship v6.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: (desktop-stack open question) Windows code signing route is unresearched; EV certificates help with SmartScreen.
refuted_or_corrected.correction:
Azure Artifact Signing (formerly Trusted Signing) went GA on Jan 12 2026.
- Price: Basic is $9.99/month for 5,000 signatures; Premium is $99.99/month.
- Eligibility: organizations in the US, Canada, EU and UK; individual developers in the US and Canada only. It needs a paid Azure subscription.
- It plugs into CI through a GitHub Action, with no hardware token.
- Since 2024, EV certificates no longer bypass SmartScreen instantly; reputation builds over consecutive signed releases either way.
- Private Trust signing is available for internal LOB or WDAC deployments.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: (desktop-stack) Tauri E2E testing on macOS is impossible because there is no WKWebView driver.
refuted_or_corrected.correction: As of Jun 2026, WebdriverIO's @wdio/tauri-service runs an embedded WebDriver server inside the app (tauri-plugin-wdio-webdriver, debug builds only). That gives E2E tests on macOS, Windows and Linux, with IPC mocking and log capture. CrabNebula's paid driver is an alternative. Only driving tauri-driver directly is limited to Windows and Linux.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: (desktop-stack) Paste injection = clipboard + synthesized Cmd/Ctrl+V + restore is the insertion method.
refuted_or_corrected.correction: Shipping Mac dictation apps (Mumbli, Dettivo) try the Accessibility API first: set kAXSelectedTextAttribute on the focused AXTextField or AXTextArea. This inserts at the cursor without touching the clipboard. They check that the attribute is settable and re-read the value, because VS Code, Google Docs and terminals report success while ignoring the write. Clipboard paste is the fallback. Refuse to insert into password fields or while secure input is active. On Windows the equivalent is UI Automation TextPattern/ValuePattern.

refuted_or_corrected.claim: (desktop-stack) No Flutter reference exists for a floating desktop pet/overlay.
refuted_or_corrected.correction: An open-source Flutter PoC, lizy-coding/dest_pets (v0.5.0, macOS validated; Windows alpha pending), renders Codex-format pet atlases in a transparent, borderless, always-on-top window. It supports drag, persisted position and an auxiliary right-click menu window. It is still a PoC: no NSPanel, no non-activating behaviour, and not production-grade. The desktop-stack conclusion that Flutter needs custom native runner code still holds.

gaps:
MASCOT ART/ANIMATION PIPELINE (researched).

Adopt the Codex pet package format as Mog's sprite contract instead of inventing one:
- Files: pet.json plus spritesheet.webp (transparent).
- Grid: 8 columns of 192x208 cells. V1 is 9 rows (1536x1872). V2 is 11 rows (1536x2288) and adds 16 look-direction poses.
- Rows: idle(6), running-right(8), running-left(8), waving(4), jumping(5), failed(8), waiting(6), running/working(6), review(6).
- Frame timings are documented, for example idle = 280/110/110/140/140/320 ms. Idle frame 0 is the reduced-motion poster.

Suggested state mapping:
- idle → idle
- listening → waiting, plus a mic-RMS overlay ring drawn in code
- transcribing/cleaning → running
- Genie thinking → review
- answer-ready → waving
- needs-input → jumping
- error → failed
- meeting-recording → idle plus a red badge drawn in code

A Flutter PoC (dest_pets) already renders these atlases. Codex tooling (the hatch-pet skill, validators) can generate and validate art, and it lets users drop in their own pets.

Rendering: draw pixel art with FilterQuality.none and integer scaling.

Optional upgrade: Rive.
- Flutter package rive 0.14.11 is stable; 0.15.0-dev adds deferred rendering. Built on the C++ runtime via rive_native.
- Runs on iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, Linux and Web.
- View-model data binding lets you bind mic level and Genie status directly to the animation.
- RiveSemantics gives screen-reader output.
- Windows falls back to Factory.flutter when there is no D3D11 device.
- Linux arm64 needs a manual build.

Lottie suits neither pixel art nor interactive state machines.

IP caveat: the attached reference art (a blue cloud robot with '>_') resembles OpenAI's Codex mascot. Commission an original 'Mog' character and run a trademark check on the name. Using Databricks brand marks needs approval.

Not verified: Rive's Factory.rive on a fully transparent, per-pixel-alpha always-on-top window. Spike this early.

END-TO-END LATENCY BUDGET (researched; no dimension produced a single budget).

Dictation path, from key-down to text:
- Mic live: under 50 ms. Capture-start clipping is an issue; see the pre-roll conflict.
- ASR, local Parakeet: 0.1-0.7 s on CPU, 0.05-0.2 s on the Apple Neural Engine.
- ASR, warm Databricks GPU: about 0.4-1.0 s.
- SLM cleanup: about 0.3-1.0 s on FMAPI pay-per-token (no published Databricks TTFT), about 0.9 s median for Apple FM on-device.
- Insertion: under 50 ms.

Target p95 is 1.0 s local and 1.5 s cloud. Show raw text first, then swap in the cleaned text. Skip the LLM for utterances under 2 s or 4 words; Dictus measured this saves the about 1.1 s Apple FM floor.

Genie path:
- Serverless warehouse cold start: 2-6 s. Pro/classic: about 4 min.
- Chat mode: 5-60+ s.
- Production with caching (GSK): 22-34 s average.
- Genie One: about 54 s average, 82 s maximum.

The Genie step must be asynchronous, with an OS notification and the mascot 'waving' when done.

Mitigation borrowed from GSK: a local cache of question→SQL/answer, plus template SQL for frequent KPIs via the Statement Execution API. This cut Genie load by 64% at a 3-4% accuracy cost.

OFFLINE / DEGRADED-MODE BEHAVIOUR (researched in part).

No dimension defines a state machine for being offline or for the token expiring mid-utterance. Proposed behaviour:
- Local Parakeet always works offline.
- Run the deterministic filler and dictionary pre-pass.
- Use the on-device SLM where available: Apple FM on macOS 26 Apple Intelligence devices; Phi Silica, then Aion Instruct from Jan 2027, on Copilot+ PCs (this needs MSIX or sparse-package identity, so it is relevant to packaging).
- Otherwise paste the raw text.
- Queue Genie questions with a visible 'will ask when online' state, and refresh tokens silently.
- Meeting mode keeps recording to the crash-safe journal and transcribes locally or later.
- Detect captive portals and corporate proxies, and honour HTTPS_PROXY and the system PAC.

MULTI-WORKSPACE / MULTI-ACCOUNT SWITCHING and GENIE SPACE SELECTION (partially covered).

The custom OAuth app is registered per Databricks account. Users who belong to several accounts (consultants, partners) need one client_id per account, or a published partner app; none was found. Requirements:
- Store a profile per workspace host: client_id, refresh token in the keychain, default Genie space, default warehouse, SLM endpoint name.
- Provide a tray switcher, with the active workspace and space shown on the mini.
- Cache GET /api/2.0/genie/spaces (page_size 100) with title, description and sample questions, and show favourites first.
- Feature-detect Genie One and Agent mode per workspace, since both are behind preview toggles.
- Admins can pin allowed workspaces and spaces through MDM, as ux-governance GOV-3 already proposes.

HOTKEY CONFLICT MATRIX (researched).

Known claims on the candidate keys:
- ChatGPT/Codex Pets and Mini: Option+Space on macOS, Win+Alt+P on Windows.
- Superwhisper: Option+Space.
- Wispr Flow: Fn on macOS, Ctrl+Win on Windows, Fn+Space or Ctrl+Win+Space for hands-free. These are exactly the defaults both Mog dimensions propose.
- Spokenly: Right-Cmd.
- macOS Fn/Globe: emoji viewer, input source or dictation, per the AppleFnUsageType setting.
- Raycast and Alfred commonly use Cmd+Space or Option+Space.

Mog needs:
- conflict detection at first run (read AppleFnUsageType, probe whether the shortcut can be registered, warn when known apps are installed);
- a one-click 'set Fn to Do Nothing' guide;
- defaults that avoid other dictation apps, such as Right-Option on macOS and Right-Alt or Ctrl+Win+M on Windows, offered as choices;
- handling of a held key across lock, sleep and fast user switching (a stuck recording).

TEXT INSERTION DETAILS (researched).

Use a tiered approach: AX kAXSelectedTextAttribute on macOS or UIA on Windows first, then clipboard paste, then a copy card.
- Verify the write took effect.
- Exclude password fields and secure input (IsSecureEventInputEnabled).
- Default terminals to clipboard paste.

Known platform conventions, not researched here: mark transient clipboard writes so clipboard managers and Windows clipboard history do not capture transcripts. On macOS that is org.nspasteboard.TransientType/ConcealedType. On Windows it is the ExcludeClipboardContentFromMonitorProcessing and CanIncludeInClipboardHistory=0 formats.

Otherwise every dictated sentence ends up in clipboard history and cloud clipboard sync, which is a data-loss-prevention issue.

TELEMETRY / OBSERVABILITY (researched).

Databricks accepts OTLP traces from any client at https://<workspace>/api/2.0/otel/v1/traces, with an X-Databricks-UC-Table-Name header. Spans land in UC Delta tables linked to an MLflow experiment.

Constraints:
- 200 traces/s per workspace.
- Writers need MODIFY and SELECT on the tables. Per-user U2M writes mean granting every Mog user MODIFY, and those users can then read all traces.
- Individual traces cannot be deleted except through SQL, which is a GDPR erasure concern.
- Storage protected by Private Link is not supported.

Recommended design:
- Per-stage latency spans: capture, ASR, SLM, insert, Genie poll.
- Content-free by default: no transcript text, only lengths, model IDs and error codes.
- Opt-in content logging for the eval golden set.
- Genie usage already lands in system.access.audit under the aibiGenie service.
- Use a separate opt-in crash reporter (e.g. Sentry) for native crashes and TCC failures.

PACKAGING / DISTRIBUTION / UPDATES (researched in part).

macOS: Developer ID, hardened runtime and a notarized DMG/PKG (the Mac App Store is ruled out by the event tap, private APIs and audio taps).

Windows: Authenticode through Azure Artifact Signing ($9.99/month; organizations in US/CA/EU/UK). Expect SmartScreen warnings until reputation builds.

MSIX vs NSIS/MSI matters:
- MSIX or a sparse package gives package identity, which the Windows on-device SLM requires.
- Machine-wide MSI is what MDM rollouts expect (the Wispr pattern).

Model weights (Parakeet about 640 MB, Whisper fallback, optional streaming model) should come from a CDN with checksums, resumable downloads and CC-BY/NVIDIA license attribution in About. Legal must resolve whether Parakeet v3 is CC-BY-4.0 or under the NVIDIA Open Model License.

Tauri updater signing-key custody, plus staged and rollback channels.

COST MODEL (computed from findings; unverified for Haiku's Databricks rate).

SLM cleanup with Llama 3.1 8B: 2.143/6.429 DBU per 1M tokens at $0.07, which is about $0.15/$0.45 per 1M. An utterance of about 400 input tokens (prompt plus glossary) and 100 output costs about $0.0001. At 200 utterances per user per day that is about $0.45 per user per month.

Haiku-class at about $1/$5 per 1M tokens: about $0.0009 per utterance, or about $4 per user per month.

Meeting summary (16k-token reduce plus chunk notes): about $0.01-0.30 per meeting, depending on the model.

ASR:
- Local Parakeet: $0.
- One always-on A10G Whisper endpoint: about $1,022/month, shared.
- Vendor gpt-transcribe: $0.0045/min (outside governance).

Genie:
- Free for U2M users until Jan 31 2027.
- Then 150 DBU per user per month free, then $0.07/DBU, plus SQL warehouse compute.
- Serverless auto-stop defaults to 10 min; the UI minimum is 5 min and the API minimum is 1 min.
- Each Genie question can wake the warehouse.

Telemetry storage is negligible.

Conclusion: for a team under about 50 users, a shared GPU ASR endpoint dominates cost by 10-100x. Local STT should be the default for economic reasons as well as latency.

ACCESSIBILITY (not deeply researched).

A never-key, non-activating mascot panel cannot be reached by keyboard-only or screen-reader users. Requirements:
- Every mascot action must also be reachable from the tray/menu-bar menu and the focusable panel.
- Post accessibility announcements on state changes (NSAccessibility announcement / UIA notification events): 'Recording', 'Genie answer ready'.
- Use RiveSemantics if Rive is adopted.
- Respect reduced motion (poster frame) and high contrast.
- Never signal state by colour alone (e.g. a red ring with no other cue).
- Earcons with volume control.
- A toggle mode as an alternative to hold-to-talk for users with RSI or motor impairments.
- Captions and transcripts in meeting mode benefit Deaf and hard-of-hearing users.
- Genie result tables must be readable by screen readers.

I18N / LANGUAGE COVERAGE (partially covered, inconsistent).

Language coverage by component:
- Parakeet v3: 25 European languages.
- Nemotron streaming in sherpa-onnx: English only confirmed.
- ai_transcribe: English and Spanish only.
- Apple FM: limited language set.
- Whisper fallback: 99 languages.
- Gemma 3 12B: listed as the multilingual SLM.
- Genie's non-English question quality: unverified.

Mog needs a per-language capability matrix that auto-routes. Example: Japanese means Whisper ASR, the Gemma SLM, and a warning that Genie may be English-tuned.

Other requirements:
- The SLM 'keep user's language' rule.
- UI strings via ARB/intl (Flutter) or i18next (React).
- RTL layout for chat cards.
- Localized consent and disclosure text, since the legal wording differs per jurisdiction.

POWER / RESOURCE BUDGET for an always-running 'mini' (partially covered).

Budgets:
- Idle RAM: Tauri about 64 MB, plus a resident Parakeet of about 0.75-0.95 GB.
- Unload the model after about 15 min idle.
- Pause animation when occluded or on battery saver. Mind macOS App Nap and Windows EcoQoS interplay with the hotkey thread.
- Rive and sprite redraw only on change; Rive 0.15 already does this.
- Defer local batch re-transcription and diarization until on AC power.

No dimension set a target. Suggested: under 150 MB idle without a model loaded, under 1% CPU idle.
cross_dimension_conflicts:
APP SHELL STACK: five dimensions point in different directions.
- The user prefers Flutter for mobile and web reach.
- desktop-stack recommends Tauri v2 (Rust + React) and explicitly not Flutter for desktop v1.
- audio-meeting recommends a Flutter shell calling a native C-ABI 'Mog Audio Core' via dart:ffi.
- local-stt recommends the sherpa_onnx Flutter package, with Tauri/transcribe-rs as the fallback.
- genie-api assumes hand-written Dart REST.
- ux-governance mentions both flutter_secure_storage and the Rust keyring crate.

Resolution path: build the hard parts as one native core in Rust or Swift/C++ behind a C ABI: hotkey tap, NSPanel, audio capture, STT and insertion. Then choose the shell by product priority: Tauri if desktop is the product, Flutter if mobile is truly near-term. iOS cannot host the overlay, hotkey or system-audio features on either stack.

MEETING AUTO-STOP AND HARD CAP: four different defaults.

| Dimension | Silence stop | Hard cap | Other |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| asr-serving | 3-5 min | about 90 min | also chunk under 1 h for ai_transcribe |
| local-stt | 10 min | 90 min | warning at 80 min |
| audio-meeting | nudge at 5 min, stop at 15 min (Granola) | 4 h (admin 1-8 h) | check-ins at 90/180/225 min; mic-release after 10 s debounce; calendar end + 5 min toast |
| ux-governance | 12 min (range 10-15) | 90 min | T-5 warning; one-click +30 min; admin up to 4 h; calendar end + 10 min |

All four agree on replacing the user's flat 60 minutes with signal-driven stopping, but the product needs one canonical policy.

GENIE SEND GATING.
- slm-cleanup auto-sends when intent=data_question and confidence is at least 0.7, otherwise it shows a chip.
- ux-governance requires a deliberate per-utterance Ask-Genie hotkey plus an optional 1-2 s preview/cancel window, with the knob only changing the default key.
- genie-api requires user-checked question checkboxes in meeting mode.
- audio-meeting adds a separate meetings-to-Genie toggle that is off by default.

Auto-send conflicts with the consent and egress model, and with the roughly 5 questions/min workspace limit.

STREAMING VS GUARDRAILS.
- slm-cleanup says to stream the cleanup tokens to hit the 1 s budget, with Haiku as the 'smart' model.
- ux-governance says Unity Gateway output guardrails (PII masking) run only on non-streaming OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions. Native Anthropic Messages format is not evaluated.

You can have low-latency streaming or Gateway output PII masking on the hot path, not both. Possible compromise: input guardrails only, plus a deterministic local PII check.

OAUTH SCOPES AND TOKEN LIFETIME.
- genie-api asks for all-apis + offline_access and wants the admin to raise the refresh TTL above the 7-day default to avoid weekly re-login.
- ux-governance asks for least-privilege scopes and short refresh TTLs to limit damage from a stolen laptop.
- The docs support only all-apis/sql/offline_access/openid/profile/email for custom apps.

Resolve with all-apis plus a moderate TTL, single-use refresh-token rotation (Beta), and a revocation runbook. Alternatively use the OBO Databricks App proxy where least privilege is mandatory, at the cost of an extra hop.

AUTH FOR ASR.
- asr-serving suggests Databricks CLI/SDK U2M.
- genie-api says the CLI client_id is not for third-party tools.

Use one Mog public client for all services.

GPU ASR ENDPOINT COST GUARD.
- ux-governance suggests scale-to-zero, a usage policy and alerts for custom Whisper/Parakeet endpoints.
- asr-serving says never use scale-to-zero for interactive use, because wake-up takes minutes (a 95 s cold call was measured) and Databricks recommends against it for production.

The choices are always-on at about $1k/month or local-first STT; scale-to-zero only suits the meeting batch path.

MEETING-MODE ASR LOCATION.
- asr-serving and local-stt default to local Parakeet, with the full-meeting re-decode done locally.
- audio-meeting says to prefer Databricks-hosted ASR on battery for meeting mode.
- ux-governance allows a policy that forces local-only STT for residency.

The battery preference requires the always-on GPU endpoint and may violate residency policy.

DIARIZATION VS BIPA.
- local-stt recommends offline diarization with speaker embeddings (pyannote Community-1, TitaNet/3D-Speaker).
- audio-meeting says never build voiceprints, citing the Otter BIPA claims that survived dismissal in 2026, and to use the you/them split from separate mic and system tracks instead.

Session-level speaker embeddings are plausibly voiceprints. Make diarization opt-in, keep embeddings in memory for that session only, and never persist them; or ship you/them labels only in v1.

RAW AUDIO RETENTION.
- audio-meeting and ux-governance delete raw audio after the transcript commits, local-only by default.
- asr-serving proposes uploading the full recording to a UC Volume for an ai_transcribe diarized pass.
- local-stt re-decodes the full recording after the meeting, which needs the audio retained until then.

Uploading to a UC Volume contradicts the local-only default and needs its own admin policy tier.

PRE-ROLL RING BUFFER VS MIC INDICATOR AND PRIVACY.
- local-stt wants a ring buffer holding the last N seconds so the first word is not clipped. That requires the mic to be open continuously.
- ux-governance UX-4 says Mog's indicator must never contradict the OS orange dot or the Windows taskbar mic icon. desktop-stack opens the mic on key-down.
- An always-open mic shows a permanent OS indicator and undermines trust.

Open the mic on key-down with a fast-start audio unit and accept about 100-200 ms of risk. Use pre-roll only in hands-free and meeting modes.

DEFAULT HOTKEYS.
- desktop-stack: Fn/Globe or Right-Option on macOS; Ctrl+Win or Right-Alt on Windows.
- ux-governance: Fn or Ctrl+Opt on macOS, Ctrl+Win on Windows, plus Ctrl+Win+G for Ask-Genie.

These match Wispr Flow's defaults exactly, so they collide on machines running Wispr. Fn collides with the macOS Globe action. Option+Space is taken by ChatGPT/Codex Mini and Superwhisper.

CLEANUP MODEL ON THE HOT PATH.
- asr-serving lists GPT OSS 20B alongside Llama 8B and Gemma 12B as a cleanup model.
- slm-cleanup shows GPT OSS 20B is reasoning-only, with about 14.7 s to the first answer token at high effort, so it is unsuitable for live cleanup. It is fine only for meeting chunk notes.

CHUNK AND PAYLOAD SIZING.
- audio-meeting's batch re-transcription uses 5-12 minute windows.
- At 16 kHz 16-bit mono PCM (1.92 MB/min), a 10-minute window is about 19 MB. That exceeds the 16 MB custom-endpoint limit and far exceeds the 4 MB FM/external limit, and the 597 s execution cap also applies.
- asr-serving and audio-meeting agree on 30 s or shorter live chunks.
- local-stt notes that Parakeet handles up to 24 min per pass locally.

Batch windows must be FLAC/Opus-encoded or go local-only.
VAD VERSION. audio-meeting says Silero v5; local-stt says v6 (v6.2.3 current). Standardize on v6.

MINIMUM OS VERSIONS. The requirements pull in different directions:
- Core Audio taps need macOS 14.2 or later; many apps require 14.4 because of early bugs.
- Some FluidAudio variants need macOS 15+ or iOS 18+.
- Apple Foundation Models needs macOS 26 with Apple Intelligence.
- The FM adapter API is end-of-life on OS 27.
- Windows process-loopback exclusion needs build 20348+.
- The Windows on-device SLM needs build 26100+ and package identity.

One support floor (e.g. macOS 14.2 and Windows 10 22H2) with per-feature gating has to be defined explicitly.

MASCOT STATE MODEL.
- ux-governance UX-3 lists about 10 states: idle, armed, listening, transcribing, cleaning, thinking, answer-ready, needs-input, error, meeting-recording.
- Its own recommendation says 8 sprite states.
- The Codex atlas format offers 9 fixed rows with different semantics (running-left/right locomotion, review, waiting).

The states need an explicit mapping, and either custom rows (e.g. 'listening', 'recording') or code-drawn overlays.

'LOCAL-ONLY' PRIVACY PROMISE VS GENIE HISTORY.
- audio-meeting and ux-governance default to local-only encrypted transcripts.
- genie-api notes that anything sent to Genie persists server-side in Genie conversation history: Genie One questions appear in the user's chat history, and they also land in audit logs.

When the knob is on, the UI must disclose that data leaves local storage and becomes visible in Databricks. Delete-conversation calls should honour Mog's retention setting.
